rule: ruling:sam-2026-10-07 claim 6 (ruling-sam-2026-10-07-p1-010): a real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides the prototype default, and the ruling's own numbered decision introduces persistence, validation, authentication and cross-service behaviour with 'such as', so the list is examples, not complete; the accessibility and progressive-enhancement duties a live GOV.UK service must meet (and a prototype need not) are such a constraint, the override reaches only as far as that duty and DR2.1 wins everywhere else (claim 5, p1-008), and DR1 already judged the same kind of difference this way (inc-137: the plain file input stays as the no-JavaScript fallback; inc-055: the server-side search stays as the no-JavaScript fallback with a live filter layered on top).
outcome: The ruling's real-constraint override covers accessibility and no-JavaScript use, and reaches only as far as that duty: every page follows Design Release 2.1 except where DR2.1 falls short of it. Origin: keep the 'Error: ' title prefix, a real 'Country of origin' label on an accessible-autocomplete over a native select that works without JavaScript, and the region code input linked to its hint and error with the error style; within that build match the prototype's visible copy, placeholder, search icon and search behaviour. Port of entry and transit countries: with JavaScript follow Design Release 2.1 (a picked transit country is added at once with no Add country button, and Remove takes it off without a page load); without JavaScript keep today's native selects, the Add country button and the Remove buttons that submit the form; keep the 'Error: ' title prefix and the visually hidden country name on each Remove. Transporters: with JavaScript the icon button filters the list in the browser and the commercial form hides its address and contact fields behind the address search and 'Enter address manually'; without JavaScript the icon button submits the term to a server-side filter and the commercial form shows its fields from the start. Upload documents: keep the 'Error: ' title prefix, the error summary at the top of the main content, the attachment error after its hint, Remove buttons naming their document and link text saying it opens in a new tab; everything else follows Design Release 2.1. CPH number: build the digit filtering and paste spreading but not the automatic focus moves. Viewed notification: the title is '<reference> - Import notification service - GOV.UK' in every state, and the journey review keeps 'Review your notification - Import notification service - GOV.UK'. Success banners (the notification list's, the deletion message and the templates pages'): no auto-dismiss; a banner stays until the trader leaves or reloads the page, and everything else about it follows Design Release 2.1.
